get.summary: What the sign-in page may offer

post.summary: Create a local account and sign in
Sign in with a local account

get.summary: Sign in through a configured provider: sends the browser to the provider
get.description: A navigation from the app's own pages, not a call: the browser is sent to the provider, which sends it back to the API once the visitor has signed in there. The API opens a session for the account the provider's identity is linked to, or creates the account where registration allows it (or the provider creates accounts), and the browser lands on return_to. It never links: a session the browser already has is closed and replaced. Anything else lands on return_to with provider_sign_in set to registration_closed, link_provider_first (the provider's verified e-mail is an account's: sign in to it, then link the provider), denied (the provider turned the visitor away), failed (nothing was proven, or the sign-in was not started: the navigation did not come from the app's own pages, the provider is not configured, or there were too many attempts) or unavailable (the provider could not be asked; trying again may work). The answer is always a redirect, never an error.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The path of the app to come back to, at most 512 characters; the home when it is not one.

get.summary: Link a configured provider to the signed-in account: sends the browser to the provider
get.description: A navigation from the app's own pages, not a call, and only on purpose (the account menu): the browser is sent to the provider, and the identity it proves is linked to the account signed in when the link started, which must still be signed in when the browser comes back. The browser lands on return_to with provider_sign_in set to linked, linked_elsewhere (the identity is linked to another account), denied, failed (as for a sign-in, and when nobody is signed in) or unavailable. No session is opened. The answer is always a redirect, never an error.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The path of the app to come back to, at most 512 characters; the home when it is not one.

get.summary: The instance's providers, and which ones the signed-in account is linked to
get.description: The providers of /config, in the same order, each with linked: true when an identity it proves already signs in to this account. An empty list when the instance has none.

put.summary: Keep the settings of the interface on the signed-in account
put.description: The language, the theme and the character, the three together, in place of the ones the account had: the front applies them after each sign-in, whatever the browser. The answer is the account as it now is. 422 invalid_request: a setting is missing or not one of its words.

get.summary: One game, as the signed-in account sees it
get.description: The catalogue's record with what the account owns of it: the entries it is owned through, as in the library, each with its playtime and missing_since, their total, and its rank among the games launched. Any game of the catalogue is answered: one that is not in the library has no entry and no rank, and one the account took out of it says so in removed. What was played of it over time is its months.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The game, by its id in the catalogue.

get.summary: What the signed-in account played of one game, month by month
get.description: The months the game was played in and the time of each, the earliest first, counted as the years of the library are: from the store's review when its year has one (exact to the month), from the daily readings otherwise. The months of a year add up to what was played of the game that year; over the same year of the library, that is its share of it, and the library's years say which days are counted at all. A game that is not in the library may have months: a review counts every game played. The day by day is the library's history.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The game, by its id in the catalogue.

get.description: The cover as an image. An instance given a data directory keeps each cover it serves: fetched from a source of the game the first time it is asked for, then served from there, with an ETag a browser sends back in If-None-Match to be answered 304 while it did not change; still served when its source does not answer or no longer has it. An instance without one fetches the cover each time it is asked for, with no ETag. Cache-Control lets the browser keep it for a week. A game without a cover answers 404 no_cover, which the browser keeps for an hour; a source that does not answer, 503 cover_unavailable, which is not kept. Until the game's store has said where its cover is, a few minutes after a sync, a cover is kept for an hour and no_cover is not kept. Any signed-in account may ask for the cover of any game; a client that asks for too many at once is answered 429.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The game, by its id in the catalogue.

get.summary: The games the signed-in account owns
get.description: One item per game, with the store entries it is owned through. Read it in parts with offset and limit; total says how many games there are in all.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The order: name (A to Z), playtime (the most played first) or last_played (the last played first). What an order cannot place comes last.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many games to skip, in that order.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most games to answer with.

get.summary: The signed-in account's library in figures
get.description: The totals the stores give, over the same games as the library. Steam gives totals and no history: what was played in a year or a week is counted from the daily readings, from tracking_since on, and is not here.

get.summary: What the signed-in account played, day by day
get.description: Playtime per day and per game since the library is read (tracking_since), over the same games as the library. A day's time is the growth of the stores' totals between two readings in a row, dated by the later one, in UTC; what a game's total was at its first reading is not split over time and is not here. Days and games with nothing played are left out.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first day to answer with, as YYYY-MM-DD; the history from its start when left out.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last day to answer with, as YYYY-MM-DD; the history to its end when left out. Before from, no day is answered.

get.summary: What the signed-in account played, year by year
get.description: Playtime per calendar year (UTC), the earliest first. A year is counted from the store's own review (source review: Steam's Year in Review, every month of it, from 2022 on) when every linked account has one, and otherwise from the daily readings (source readings: the growth of the totals, from the first reading on). A year before the first reading is counted from the reviews of the accounts that have one. first_day and last_day say the days a year covers, and whole whether that is all of it. A review counts every game played, owned or not; the readings count the games of the library.

get.summary: What the signed-in account played in one month, game by game
get.description: The games played in a month and the time of each, the most played first, counted as the month's year is in the years of the library: from the store's review (every game played, owned or not, which is why each comes with its name) or from the daily readings (the games of the library, over first_day to last_day). A month nothing counts, before the first reading in a year with no review or still to come, is answered with no source and no game.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: The month, as YYYY-MM, in UTC.

delete.summary: Take a game its store no longer lists out of the library
delete.description: Takes out every entry of the game that is flagged as missing (missing_since); an entry a store still lists stays, and the game with it. 409 still_listed when no entry is missing: only a game its store no longer lists is taken out. What was known of the game is kept, and it stays out: no sync puts it back. If its store lists it again, the removed games say so (back_since), and its owner puts it back or dismisses that notice.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The game, by its id in the catalogue.

put.summary: Put a game back in the library
put.description: Puts back everything the account took out of the game, whether its store lists it again or not: an entry the store does not list comes back flagged as missing. 404 not_removed when nothing of the game was taken out.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The game, by its id in the catalogue.

get.summary: The games the signed-in account took out of its library
get.description: One item per game, by name, with the entries taken out. back_since is the notice to show: a store lists the game again since that date, and the notice was not dismissed. A game taken out is not in the library, its figures or its history; a store's review of a year still counts what was played of it.

delete.summary: Dismiss the notice that a removed game is back
delete.description: For good: the game stays out, and nothing its store says later raises the notice again. It can still be put back. 404 not_removed when nothing of the game was taken out, 409 not_back when no store lists it again. Dismissing a notice twice changes nothing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The game, by its id in the catalogue.

get.summary: The store accounts linked to the signed-in account, and where the reading of each stands

delete.description: Forgets everything that was read from it: the library it gave, its history and the store's answers. It cannot be undone; linking the same store account again starts from nothing.

post.summary: Read a linked account's library from its store, now
post.description: The library is read every day without being asked; this reads it at once, and answers when it is done, which takes the time the store takes to answer. A store that cannot be read is not an error of the request: the answer is the sync with its outcome, failed, and why. Once started, the sync goes on to its end even when the request is given up. 409 sync_in_progress: that account is being read right now. 429 too_many_requests, with Retry-After: it was read less than a minute ago. No sync takes a game out of the library: a game the store no longer lists is flagged (missing_since on its library entry).

get.summary: Link a Steam account: sends the browser to Steam
get.description: A navigation from the app's own pages, not a call: the browser is sent to Steam ("Sign in through Steam"), which sends it back to the app once the visitor has proven a Steam account is theirs. The browser then lands on return_to with the outcome in the steam_link parameter: linked, linked_elsewhere (that Steam account is linked to another account of this instance), failed (nothing was proven) or unavailable (Steam could not be asked to confirm; trying again may work). It links a library and never opens a session.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The path of the app to come back to, at most 512 characters; the home when it is not one.

put.summary: Give a linked account the owner's own key of the store
put.description: Replaces the key the account had, if any. From then on every sync of that account reads it with this key, and only this one: a key the store refuses makes the sync fail (refused, own_key true), never a reading with the instance's key. The store is not asked here: the next sync says whether it takes the key. The key is stored encrypted and never answered. 400 invalid_key: not in the shape of the store's keys (Steam: a Steam Web API key, letters and digits). 503 keys_unavailable: this instance cannot keep a key.

delete.summary: Take the owner's own key away from a linked account
delete.description: The account is read with the instance's key again. Removing a key that is not there changes nothing.
